details: This record is the commemorative monument at the eastern end of Brickdam, not a site of the 1763 rebellion itself or the distinct nearby Independence Arch. description: Remains of a Dutch trading outpost on a small island near the Mazaruni–Cuyuni confluence in Guyana. The National Trust dates the permanent Dutch building to approximately 1616.
description_zh: 凯克欧弗阿尔堡位于圭亚那马扎鲁尼河与库尤尼河交汇处附近的小岛上，现存遗迹属于荷兰贸易据点。圭亚那国家信托机构将荷兰永久建筑的年代记为约1616年。
details: The record covers the military fort remains on the islet. The National Trust describes a possible earlier outpost without an established builder, followed by the Dutch permanent building. The same named fort’s Wikidata point agrees with the published site coordinate of Museu Marítimo EXEA and is close to published camera-position metadata from the islet. Atlas of Mutual Heritage displays a different position for the fort. The chosen point is the Wikidata Earth reference point, not the photo location, Atlas point or a survey of individual remains.

description: A colonial archaeological complex on the upper Berbice River in Guyana. The National Trust distinguishes an earlier trading post, a relocation in 1629–1630, and later rebuilding at a nearby location.
description_zh: 拿骚堡是圭亚那伯比斯河上游的殖民时期考古遗址群。国家信托机构区分了早期贸易据点、1629至1630年的迁址，以及后续在附近展开的重建。
details: This record is the named archaeological complex of Upper Berbice. It does not identify the Ghanaian fort of the same name or a single structure preserved at every stage of the complex. Wikidata and the Atlas of Mutual Heritage show different reference points about 0.57 km apart for the same named complex. The adopted Wikidata point represents the complex for navigation; the sources do not fix it to a particular fort building or phase.

description: A brick Dutch fort on Fort Island in the Essequibo River, Guyana. The National Trust dates completion of the brick fort to 1744 and describes an earlier timber predecessor.

details: This record covers the brick fort. The adjacent Court of Policy building is part of the joint UNESCO Tentative List property. The public GLSC gazetteer records Zeelandia, Fort as a named Locality on the east side of Fort Island. The project's representative point is the WGS84 geometry of that entry, with no adopted positional accuracy. It does not locate an excavated feature, entrance or legal boundary. The distinct DMS fields, Wikidata and Atlas points are retained as source context and are not substituted or averaged.

description: The present Gothic Revival Anglican cathedral on North Road, Georgetown, Guyana. The National Trust describes it as the fourth cathedral building and gives 8 November 1894 as its consecration date.
description_zh: 乔治敦圣乔治座堂是圭亚那乔治敦北路的一座哥特复兴式圣公会建筑。国家信托机构记载现建筑为第四座座堂，于1894年11月8日祝圣。
details: This record covers the standing cathedral, which is distinct from earlier chapels and cathedral buildings, and from the parish’s institutional foundation. The source identifies the historic building, but Wikidata Q4256302’s sole coordinate declares negative precision in the retrieved revisions. No representative point is adopted and no neighbourhood point is substituted.

description: The historic steel-framed market hall on the Demerara waterfront in Georgetown, Guyana. The present hall opened on 1 November 1881 and retains a prominent clock tower.

details: This record is the current market hall. Earlier market activity and the former market building are distinct stages at the same site. Georgetown City Hall is a separate building. The same market hall has a Wikidata reference point with a coarse angular precision declaration of about 0.0090°. The numeric point is not a surveyed outline or entrance.
